Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. 26	// RunOnce rebuilds the payload of all memos.
27	func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) {
28		// Process memos in batches to avoid loading all memos into memory at once
29		const batchSize = 100
30		offset := 0
31		processed := 0
32

35			memos, err := r.Store.ListMemos(ctx, &store.FindMemo{

44			// Break if no more memos
45			if len(memos) == 0 {
46				break
47			}
48	
49			// Process batch
50			batchSuccessCount := 0
51			for _, memo := range memos {
52				if err := RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, r.MarkdownService); err != nil {
53					slog.Error("failed to rebuild memo payload", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
54					continue
55				}
56				if err := r.Store.UpdateMemo(ctx, &store.UpdateMemo{
57					ID:      memo.ID,

59				}); err != nil {

72	}

3	A production-ready, GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler for Go.

5	## Features
6	
7	- **Standard Cron Syntax**: Supports both 5-field and 6-field (with seconds) cron expressions
8	- **Timezone-Aware**: Explicit timezone handling to avoid DST surprises
9	- **Middleware Pattern**: Composable job wrappers for logging, metrics, panic recovery, timeouts
10	- **Graceful Shutdown**: Jobs complete cleanly or cancel when context expires
11	- **Zero Dependencies**: Core functionality uses only the standard library
12	- **Type-Safe**: Strong typing with clear error messages
13	- **Well-Tested**: Comprehensive test coverage
14	
15	## Installation
16	
17	This package is included with Memos. No separate installation required.
18	
19	## Quick Start
20	
21	```go
22	package main
23	
24	import (
25	    "context"
26	    "fmt"
27	    "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"
28	)
29	
30	func main() {
31	    s := scheduler.New()
32	
33	    s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
34	        Name:     "daily-cleanup",
35	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *", // 2 AM daily
36	        Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
37	            fmt.Println("Running cleanup...")
38	            return nil
39	        },
40	    })
41	
42	    s.Start()
43	    defer s.Stop(context.Background())
44	
45	    // Keep running...
46	    select {}
47	}
48	```
49	
50	## Cron Expression Format
51	
52	### 5-Field Format (Standard)
53	```
54	┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
55	│ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
56	│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
57	│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
58	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7) (Sunday = 0 or 7)
59	│ │ │ │ │
60	* * * * *
61	```
62	
63	### 6-Field Format (With Seconds)
64	```
65	┌───────────── second (0 - 59)
66	│ ┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
67	│ │ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
68	│ │ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
69	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
70	│ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7)
71	│ │ │ │ │ │
72	* * * * * *
73	```
74	
75	### Special Characters
76	
77	- `*` - Any value (every minute, every hour, etc.)
78	- `,` - List of values: `1,15,30` (1st, 15th, and 30th)
79	- `-` - Range: `9-17` (9 AM through 5 PM)
80	- `/` - Step: `*/15` (every 15 units)
81	
82	### Common Examples
83	
84	| Schedule | Description |
85	|----------|-------------|
86	| `* * * * *` | Every minute |
87	| `0 * * * *` | Every hour |
88	| `0 0 * * *` | Daily at midnight |
89	| `0 9 * * 1-5` | Weekdays at 9 AM |
90	| `*/15 * * * *` | Every 15 minutes |
91	| `0 0 1 * *` | First day of every month |
92	| `0 0 * * 0` | Every Sunday at midnight |
93	| `30 14 * * *` | Every day at 2:30 PM |
94	
95	## Timezone Support
96	
97	```go
98	// Global timezone for all jobs
99	s := scheduler.New(
100	    scheduler.WithTimezone("America/New_York"),
101	)
102	
103	// Per-job timezone (overrides global)
104	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
105	    Name:     "tokyo-report",
106	    Schedule: "0 9 * * *", // 9 AM Tokyo time
107	    Timezone: "Asia/Tokyo",
108	    Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
109	        // Runs at 9 AM in Tokyo
110	        return nil
111	    },
112	})
113	```
114	
115	**Important**: Always use IANA timezone names (`America/New_York`, not `EST`).
116	
117	## Middleware
118	
119	Middleware wraps job handlers to add cross-cutting behavior. Multiple middleware can be chained together.
120	
121	### Built-in Middleware
122	
123	#### Recovery (Panic Handling)
124	
125	```go
126	s := scheduler.New(
127	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
128	        scheduler.Recovery(func(jobName string, r interface{}) {
129	            log.Printf("Job %s panicked: %v", jobName, r)
130	        }),
131	    ),
132	)
133	```
134	
135	#### Logging
136	
137	```go
138	type Logger interface {
139	    Info(msg string, args ...interface{})
140	    Error(msg string, args ...interface{})
141	}
142	
143	s := scheduler.New(
144	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
145	        scheduler.Logging(myLogger),
146	    ),
147	)
148	```
149	
150	#### Timeout
151	
152	```go
153	s := scheduler.New(
154	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
155	        scheduler.Timeout(5 * time.Minute),
156	    ),
157	)
158	```
159	
160	### Combining Middleware
161	
162	```go
163	s := scheduler.New(
164	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
165	        scheduler.Recovery(panicHandler),
166	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
167	        scheduler.Timeout(10 * time.Minute),
168	    ),
169	)
170	```
171	
172	**Order matters**: Middleware are applied left-to-right. In the example above:
173	1. Recovery (outermost) catches panics from everything
174	2. Logging logs the execution
175	3. Timeout (innermost) wraps the actual handler
176	
177	### Custom Middleware
178	
179	```go
180	func Metrics(recorder MetricsRecorder) scheduler.Middleware {
181	    return func(next scheduler.JobHandler) scheduler.JobHandler {
182	        return func(ctx context.Context) error {
183	            start := time.Now()
184	            err := next(ctx)
185	            duration := time.Since(start)
186	
187	            jobName := scheduler.GetJobName(ctx)
188	            recorder.Record(jobName, duration, err)
189	
190	            return err
191	        }
192	    }
193	}
194	```
195	
196	## Graceful Shutdown
197	
198	Always use `Stop()` with a context to allow jobs to finish cleanly:
199	
200	```go
201	// Give jobs up to 30 seconds to complete
202	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
203	defer cancel()
204	
205	if err := s.Stop(ctx); err != nil {
206	    log.Printf("Shutdown error: %v", err)
207	}
208	```
209	
210	Jobs should respect context cancellation:
211	
212	```go
213	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
214	    for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
215	        select {
216	        case <-ctx.Done():
217	            return ctx.Err() // Canceled
218	        default:
219	            // Do work
220	        }
221	    }
222	    return nil
223	}
224	```
225	
226	## Best Practices
227	
228	### 1. Always Name Your Jobs
229	
230	Names are used for logging, metrics, and debugging:
231	
232	```go
233	Name: "user-cleanup-job" // Good
234	Name: "job1"             // Bad
235	```
236	
237	### 2. Add Descriptions and Tags
238	
239	```go
240	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
241	    Name:        "stale-session-cleanup",
242	    Description: "Removes user sessions older than 30 days",
243	    Tags:        []string{"maintenance", "security"},
244	    Schedule:    "0 3 * * *",
245	    Handler:     cleanupSessions,
246	})
247	```
248	
249	### 3. Use Appropriate Middleware
250	
251	Always include Recovery and Logging in production:
252	
253	```go
254	scheduler.New(
255	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
256	        scheduler.Recovery(logPanic),
257	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
258	    ),
259	)
260	```
261	
262	### 4. Avoid Scheduling Exactly on the Hour
263	
264	Many systems schedule jobs at `:00`, causing load spikes. Stagger your jobs:
265	
266	```go
267	"5 2 * * *"  // 2:05 AM (good)
268	"0 2 * * *"  // 2:00 AM (often overloaded)
269	```
270	
271	### 5. Make Jobs Idempotent
272	
273	Jobs may run multiple times (crash recovery, etc.). Design them to be safely re-runnable:
274	
275	```go
276	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
277	    // Use unique constraint or check-before-insert
278	    db.Exec("INSERT IGNORE INTO processed_items ...")
279	    return nil
280	}
281	```
282	
283	### 6. Handle Timezones Explicitly
284	
285	Always specify timezone for business-hour jobs:
286	
287	```go
288	Timezone: "America/New_York" // Good
289	// Timezone: ""              // Bad (defaults to UTC)
290	```
291	
292	### 7. Test Your Cron Expressions
293	
294	Use a cron expression calculator before deploying:
295	- [crontab.guru](https://crontab.guru/)
296	- Write unit tests with the parser
297	
298	## Testing Jobs
299	
300	Test job handlers independently of the scheduler:
301	
302	```go
303	func TestCleanupJob(t *testing.T) {
304	    ctx := context.Background()
305	
306	    err := cleanupHandler(ctx)
307	    if err != nil {
308	        t.Fatalf("cleanup failed: %v", err)
309	    }
310	
311	    // Verify cleanup occurred
312	}
313	```
314	
315	Test schedule parsing:
316	
317	```go
318	func TestScheduleParsing(t *testing.T) {
319	    job := &scheduler.Job{
320	        Name:     "test",
321	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *",
322	        Handler:  func(ctx context.Context) error { return nil },
323	    }
324	
325	    if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
326	        t.Fatalf("invalid job: %v", err)
327	    }
328	}
329	```

29	func (r *Runner) Run(ctx context.Context) {
30		ticker := time.NewTicker(runnerInterval)
31		defer ticker.Stop()
32	
33		for {
34			select {
35			case <-ticker.C:
36				r.RunOnce(ctx)

47	func (r *Runner) CheckAndPresign(ctx context.Context) {
48		instanceStorageSetting, err := r.Store.GetInstanceStorageSetting(ctx)
49		if err != nil {
50			return
51		}
52	
53		s3StorageType := storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3
54		// Limit attachments to a reasonable batch size
55		const batchSize = 100
56		offset := 0
57	
58		for {
59			limit := batchSize
60			attachments, err := r.Store.ListAttachments(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{
61				GetBlob:     false,
62				StorageType: &s3StorageType,
63				Limit:       &limit,
64				Offset:      &offset,
65			})
66			if err != nil {
67				slog.Error("Failed to list attachments for presigning", "error", err)
68				return
69			}
70	
71			// Break if no more attachments
72			if len(attachments) == 0 {
73				break
74			}
75	
76			// Process batch of attachments
77			presignCount := 0
78			for _, attachment := range attachments {
79				payload := cloneAttachmentPayload(attachment.Payload)
80				s3ObjectPayload := payload.GetS3Object()
81				if s3ObjectPayload == nil {
82					continue
83				}
84	
85				if s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime != nil {
86					// Skip if the presigned URL is still valid for the next 4 days.
87					// The expiration time is set to 5 days.
88					if time.Now().Before(s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime.AsTime().Add(4 * 24 * time.Hour)) {
89						continue
90					}
91				}
92	
93				s3Config := instanceStorageSetting.GetS3Config()
94				if s3ObjectPayload.S3Config != nil {
95					s3Config = s3ObjectPayload.S3Config
96				}
97				if s3Config == nil {
98					slog.Error("S3 config is not found")
99					continue
100				}
101	
102				s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(ctx, s3Config)
103				if err != nil {
104					slog.Error("Failed to create S3 client", "error", err)
105					continue
106				}
107	
108				presignURL, err := s3Client.PresignGetObject(ctx, s3ObjectPayload.Key)
109				if err != nil {
110					slog.Error("Failed to presign URL", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
111					continue
112				}
113	
114				s3ObjectPayload.S3Config = s3Config
115				s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime = timestamppb.New(time.Now())
116				if err := r.Store.UpdateAttachment(ctx, &store.UpdateAttachment{
117					ID:        attachment.ID,
118					Reference: &presignURL,
119					Payload:   payload,
120				}); err != nil {
121					slog.Error("Failed to update attachment", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
122					continue
123				}
124				presignCount++
125			}
126	
127			slog.Info("Presigned batch of S3 attachments", "batchSize", len(attachments), "presigned", presignCount)
128	
129			// Move to next batch
130			offset += len(attachments)
131		}
132	}

44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})
70	
71		// Serve frontend static files.
72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
82		fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
83	
84		// Create and register RSS routes (needs markdown service from apiV1Service).
85		rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
86	
87		// Register gRPC gateway as api v1 (includes SSE endpoint on CORS-enabled group).
88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")
90		}
91	
92		mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
95		}
96		mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
97	
98		return s, nil
99	}

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}

134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {
147			slog.Error("failed to close database", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
148		}
149	
150		slog.Info("memos stopped properly")
151	}

153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160	
161		// Create and start S3 presign runner
162		s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164	
165		// Start continuous S3 presign runner
166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {
168			defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")
171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}

176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {
178			if cancelFunc != nil {
179				cancelFunc()
180			}
181		}
182	}

184	func (s *Server) waitBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
185		done := make(chan struct{})
186		go func() {
187			s.backgroundRunnerWG.Wait()
188			close(done)
189		}()
190	
191		select {
192		case <-done:
193		case <-ctx.Done():
194			select {
195			case <-done:
196				return
197			default:
198			}
199			slog.Error("failed to stop background runners", slog.String("error", ctx.Err().Error()))
200		}
201	}

203	func (s *Server) closeLongLivedConnections() {
204		// Long-lived SSE requests do not finish on their own during http.Server.Shutdown.
205		if s.sseHub != nil {
206			s.sseHub.Close()
207		}

210	func (s *Server) shutdownHTTPServer(ctx context.Context) {
211		if s.httpServer == nil {
212			return
213		}
214		if err := s.httpServer.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
215			slog.Error("failed to shutdown server", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
216			if closeErr := s.httpServer.Close(); closeErr != nil && closeErr != http.ErrServerClosed {
217				slog.Error("failed to close server", slog.String("error", closeErr.Error()))
218			}
219		}
220	}

222	func (s *Server) getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx context.Context) (*storepb.InstanceBasicSetting, error) {
223		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
224		if err != nil {
225			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
226		}
227		modified := false
228		if instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey == "" {
229			instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey = uuid.NewString()
230			modified = true
231		}
232		if modified {
233			instanceSetting, err := s.Store.UpsertInstanceSetting(ctx, &storepb.InstanceSetting{
234				Key:   storepb.InstanceSettingKey_BASIC,
235				Value: &storepb.InstanceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: instanceBasicSetting},
236			})
237			if err != nil {
238				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert instance setting")
239			}
240			instanceBasicSetting = instanceSetting.GetBasicSetting()
241		}

3	import (
4		"context"

11		"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
12	)
13	
14	type Runner struct {
15		Store           *store.Store
16		MarkdownService markdown.Service
17	}
18	
19	func NewRunner(store *store.Store, markdownService markdown.Service) *Runner {
20		return &Runner{
21			Store:           store,
22			MarkdownService: markdownService,
23		}
24	}
25	
26	// RunOnce rebuilds the payload of all memos.
27	func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) {
28		// Process memos in batches to avoid loading all memos into memory at once
29		const batchSize = 100
30		offset := 0
31		processed := 0
32	
33		for {
34			limit := batchSize
35			memos, err := r.Store.ListMemos(ctx, &store.FindMemo{
36				Limit:  &limit,
37				Offset: &offset,
38			})
39			if err != nil {
40				slog.Error("failed to list memos", "err", err)
41				return
42			}
43	
44			// Break if no more memos
45			if len(memos) == 0 {
46				break
47			}
48	
49			// Process batch
50			batchSuccessCount := 0
51			for _, memo := range memos {
52				if err := RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, r.MarkdownService); err != nil {
53					slog.Error("failed to rebuild memo payload", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
54					continue
55				}
56				if err := r.Store.UpdateMemo(ctx, &store.UpdateMemo{
57					ID:      memo.ID,
58					Payload: memo.Payload,
59				}); err != nil {
60					slog.Error("failed to update memo", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
61					continue
62				}
63				batchSuccessCount++
64			}
65	
66			processed += len(memos)
67			slog.Info("Processed memo batch", "batchSize", len(memos), "successCount", batchSuccessCount, "totalProcessed", processed)
68	
69			// Move to next batch
70			offset += len(memos)
71		}
72	}
73	
74	func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error {
75		if memo.Payload == nil {
76			memo.Payload = &storepb.MemoPayload{}
77		}
78	
79		// Use goldmark service to extract all metadata in a single pass (more efficient)
80		data, err := markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))
81		if err != nil {
82			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to extract markdown metadata")
83		}
84	
85		memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
86		memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
87		return nil
88	}

2	
3	A production-ready, GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler for Go.
4	
5	## Features
6	
7	- **Standard Cron Syntax**: Supports both 5-field and 6-field (with seconds) cron expressions
8	- **Timezone-Aware**: Explicit timezone handling to avoid DST surprises
9	- **Middleware Pattern**: Composable job wrappers for logging, metrics, panic recovery, timeouts
10	- **Graceful Shutdown**: Jobs complete cleanly or cancel when context expires
11	- **Zero Dependencies**: Core functionality uses only the standard library
12	- **Type-Safe**: Strong typing with clear error messages
13	- **Well-Tested**: Comprehensive test coverage
14	
15	## Installation
16	
17	This package is included with Memos. No separate installation required.
18	
19	## Quick Start
20	
21	```go
22	package main
23	
24	import (
25	    "context"
26	    "fmt"
27	    "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"
28	)
29	
30	func main() {
31	    s := scheduler.New()
32	
33	    s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
34	        Name:     "daily-cleanup",
35	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *", // 2 AM daily
36	        Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
37	            fmt.Println("Running cleanup...")
38	            return nil
39	        },
40	    })
41	
42	    s.Start()
43	    defer s.Stop(context.Background())
44	
45	    // Keep running...
46	    select {}
47	}
48	```
49	
50	## Cron Expression Format
51	
52	### 5-Field Format (Standard)
53	```
54	┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
55	│ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
56	│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
57	│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
58	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7) (Sunday = 0 or 7)
59	│ │ │ │ │
60	* * * * *
61	```
62	
63	### 6-Field Format (With Seconds)
64	```
65	┌───────────── second (0 - 59)
66	│ ┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
67	│ │ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
68	│ │ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
69	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
70	│ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7)
71	│ │ │ │ │ │
72	* * * * * *
73	```
74	
75	### Special Characters
76	
77	- `*` - Any value (every minute, every hour, etc.)
78	- `,` - List of values: `1,15,30` (1st, 15th, and 30th)
79	- `-` - Range: `9-17` (9 AM through 5 PM)
80	- `/` - Step: `*/15` (every 15 units)
81	
82	### Common Examples
83	
84	| Schedule | Description |
85	|----------|-------------|
86	| `* * * * *` | Every minute |
87	| `0 * * * *` | Every hour |
88	| `0 0 * * *` | Daily at midnight |
89	| `0 9 * * 1-5` | Weekdays at 9 AM |
90	| `*/15 * * * *` | Every 15 minutes |
91	| `0 0 1 * *` | First day of every month |
92	| `0 0 * * 0` | Every Sunday at midnight |
93	| `30 14 * * *` | Every day at 2:30 PM |
94	
95	## Timezone Support
96	
97	```go
98	// Global timezone for all jobs
99	s := scheduler.New(
100	    scheduler.WithTimezone("America/New_York"),
101	)
102	
103	// Per-job timezone (overrides global)
104	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
105	    Name:     "tokyo-report",
106	    Schedule: "0 9 * * *", // 9 AM Tokyo time
107	    Timezone: "Asia/Tokyo",
108	    Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
109	        // Runs at 9 AM in Tokyo
110	        return nil
111	    },
112	})
113	```
114	
115	**Important**: Always use IANA timezone names (`America/New_York`, not `EST`).
116	
117	## Middleware
118	
119	Middleware wraps job handlers to add cross-cutting behavior. Multiple middleware can be chained together.
120	
121	### Built-in Middleware
122	
123	#### Recovery (Panic Handling)
124	
125	```go
126	s := scheduler.New(
127	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
128	        scheduler.Recovery(func(jobName string, r interface{}) {
129	            log.Printf("Job %s panicked: %v", jobName, r)
130	        }),
131	    ),
132	)
133	```
134	
135	#### Logging
136	
137	```go
138	type Logger interface {
139	    Info(msg string, args ...interface{})
140	    Error(msg string, args ...interface{})
141	}
142	
143	s := scheduler.New(
144	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
145	        scheduler.Logging(myLogger),
146	    ),
147	)
148	```
149	
150	#### Timeout
151	
152	```go
153	s := scheduler.New(
154	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
155	        scheduler.Timeout(5 * time.Minute),
156	    ),
157	)
158	```
159	
160	### Combining Middleware
161	
162	```go
163	s := scheduler.New(
164	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
165	        scheduler.Recovery(panicHandler),
166	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
167	        scheduler.Timeout(10 * time.Minute),
168	    ),
169	)
170	```
171	
172	**Order matters**: Middleware are applied left-to-right. In the example above:
173	1. Recovery (outermost) catches panics from everything
174	2. Logging logs the execution
175	3. Timeout (innermost) wraps the actual handler
176	
177	### Custom Middleware
178	
179	```go
180	func Metrics(recorder MetricsRecorder) scheduler.Middleware {
181	    return func(next scheduler.JobHandler) scheduler.JobHandler {
182	        return func(ctx context.Context) error {
183	            start := time.Now()
184	            err := next(ctx)
185	            duration := time.Since(start)
186	
187	            jobName := scheduler.GetJobName(ctx)
188	            recorder.Record(jobName, duration, err)
189	
190	            return err
191	        }
192	    }
193	}
194	```
195	
196	## Graceful Shutdown
197	
198	Always use `Stop()` with a context to allow jobs to finish cleanly:
199	
200	```go
201	// Give jobs up to 30 seconds to complete
202	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
203	defer cancel()
204	
205	if err := s.Stop(ctx); err != nil {
206	    log.Printf("Shutdown error: %v", err)
207	}
208	```
209	
210	Jobs should respect context cancellation:
211	
212	```go
213	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
214	    for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
215	        select {
216	        case <-ctx.Done():
217	            return ctx.Err() // Canceled
218	        default:
219	            // Do work
220	        }
221	    }
222	    return nil
223	}
224	```

226	## Best Practices
227	
228	### 1. Always Name Your Jobs
229	
230	Names are used for logging, metrics, and debugging:
231	
232	```go
233	Name: "user-cleanup-job" // Good
234	Name: "job1"             // Bad
235	```
236	
237	### 2. Add Descriptions and Tags
238	
239	```go
240	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
241	    Name:        "stale-session-cleanup",
242	    Description: "Removes user sessions older than 30 days",
243	    Tags:        []string{"maintenance", "security"},
244	    Schedule:    "0 3 * * *",
245	    Handler:     cleanupSessions,
246	})
247	```
248	
249	### 3. Use Appropriate Middleware
250	
251	Always include Recovery and Logging in production:
252	
253	```go
254	scheduler.New(
255	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
256	        scheduler.Recovery(logPanic),
257	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
258	    ),
259	)
260	```
261	
262	### 4. Avoid Scheduling Exactly on the Hour
263	
264	Many systems schedule jobs at `:00`, causing load spikes. Stagger your jobs:
265	
266	```go
267	"5 2 * * *"  // 2:05 AM (good)
268	"0 2 * * *"  // 2:00 AM (often overloaded)
269	```
270	
271	### 5. Make Jobs Idempotent
272	
273	Jobs may run multiple times (crash recovery, etc.). Design them to be safely re-runnable:
274	
275	```go
276	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
277	    // Use unique constraint or check-before-insert
278	    db.Exec("INSERT IGNORE INTO processed_items ...")
279	    return nil
280	}
281	```
282	
283	### 6. Handle Timezones Explicitly
284	
285	Always specify timezone for business-hour jobs:
286	
287	```go
288	Timezone: "America/New_York" // Good
289	// Timezone: ""              // Bad (defaults to UTC)
290	```
291	
292	### 7. Test Your Cron Expressions
293	
294	Use a cron expression calculator before deploying:
295	- [crontab.guru](https://crontab.guru/)
296	- Write unit tests with the parser
297	
298	## Testing Jobs
299	
300	Test job handlers independently of the scheduler:
301	
302	```go
303	func TestCleanupJob(t *testing.T) {
304	    ctx := context.Background()
305	
306	    err := cleanupHandler(ctx)
307	    if err != nil {
308	        t.Fatalf("cleanup failed: %v", err)
309	    }
310	
311	    // Verify cleanup occurred
312	}
313	```
314	
315	Test schedule parsing:
316	
317	```go
318	func TestScheduleParsing(t *testing.T) {
319	    job := &scheduler.Job{
320	        Name:     "test",
321	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *",
322	        Handler:  func(ctx context.Context) error { return nil },
323	    }
324	
325	    if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
326	        t.Fatalf("invalid job: %v", err)
327	    }
328	}
329	```
330	
331	## Comparison to Other Solutions
332	
333	| Feature | scheduler | robfig/cron | github.com/go-co-op/gocron |
334	|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------------------|
335	| Standard cron syntax | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

344	
345	See [example_test.go](./example_test.go) for comprehensive examples.

47	func (r *Runner) CheckAndPresign(ctx context.Context) {
48		instanceStorageSetting, err := r.Store.GetInstanceStorageSetting(ctx)
49		if err != nil {
50			return
51		}
52	
53		s3StorageType := storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3

55		const batchSize = 100
56		offset := 0
57	
58		for {
59			limit := batchSize
60			attachments, err := r.Store.ListAttachments(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{
61				GetBlob:     false,
62				StorageType: &s3StorageType,
63				Limit:       &limit,
64				Offset:      &offset,
65			})
66			if err != nil {
67				slog.Error("Failed to list attachments for presigning", "error", err)
68				return
69			}
70	
71			// Break if no more attachments
72			if len(attachments) == 0 {
73				break
74			}
75	
76			// Process batch of attachments
77			presignCount := 0
78			for _, attachment := range attachments {
79				payload := cloneAttachmentPayload(attachment.Payload)
80				s3ObjectPayload := payload.GetS3Object()
81				if s3ObjectPayload == nil {
82					continue
83				}
84	
85				if s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime != nil {
86					// Skip if the presigned URL is still valid for the next 4 days.
87					// The expiration time is set to 5 days.
88					if time.Now().Before(s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime.AsTime().Add(4 * 24 * time.Hour)) {
89						continue
90					}
91				}
92	
93				s3Config := instanceStorageSetting.GetS3Config()
94				if s3ObjectPayload.S3Config != nil {
95					s3Config = s3ObjectPayload.S3Config
96				}
97				if s3Config == nil {
98					slog.Error("S3 config is not found")

100				}
101	
102				s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(ctx, s3Config)
103				if err != nil {
104					slog.Error("Failed to create S3 client", "error", err)

106				}
107	
108				presignURL, err := s3Client.PresignGetObject(ctx, s3ObjectPayload.Key)
109				if err != nil {
110					slog.Error("Failed to presign URL", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
111					continue
112				}
113	
114				s3ObjectPayload.S3Config = s3Config
115				s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime = timestamppb.New(time.Now())

118					Reference: &presignURL,
119					Payload:   payload,
120				}); err != nil {
121					slog.Error("Failed to update attachment", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
122					continue
123				}

125			}
126	
127			slog.Info("Presigned batch of S3 attachments", "batchSize", len(attachments), "presigned", presignCount)
128	
129			// Move to next batch
130			offset += len(attachments)
131		}
132	}

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {

111		if err != nil {

113		}

117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}

123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}

14	type Runner struct {
15		Store           *store.Store
16		MarkdownService markdown.Service
17	}
18	
19	func NewRunner(store *store.Store, markdownService markdown.Service) *Runner {
20		return &Runner{
21			Store:           store,
22			MarkdownService: markdownService,
23		}
24	}

26	// RunOnce rebuilds the payload of all memos.
27	func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) {
28		// Process memos in batches to avoid loading all memos into memory at once
29		const batchSize = 100
30		offset := 0
31		processed := 0
32	
33		for {
34			limit := batchSize
35			memos, err := r.Store.ListMemos(ctx, &store.FindMemo{
36				Limit:  &limit,
37				Offset: &offset,
38			})
39			if err != nil {
40				slog.Error("failed to list memos", "err", err)
41				return
42			}
43	
44			// Break if no more memos
45			if len(memos) == 0 {
46				break
47			}
48	
49			// Process batch
50			batchSuccessCount := 0
51			for _, memo := range memos {
52				if err := RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, r.MarkdownService); err != nil {
53					slog.Error("failed to rebuild memo payload", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
54					continue
55				}
56				if err := r.Store.UpdateMemo(ctx, &store.UpdateMemo{
57					ID:      memo.ID,
58					Payload: memo.Payload,
59				}); err != nil {
60					slog.Error("failed to update memo", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
61					continue
62				}
63				batchSuccessCount++
64			}
65	
66			processed += len(memos)
67			slog.Info("Processed memo batch", "batchSize", len(memos), "successCount", batchSuccessCount, "totalProcessed", processed)
68	
69			// Move to next batch
70			offset += len(memos)
71		}
72	}
73	
74	func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error {
75		if memo.Payload == nil {
76			memo.Payload = &storepb.MemoPayload{}
77		}
78	
79		// Use goldmark service to extract all metadata in a single pass (more efficient)
80		data, err := markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))
81		if err != nil {
82			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to extract markdown metadata")
83		}
84	
85		memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
86		memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
87		return nil
88	}

2	
3	A production-ready, GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler for Go.
4	
5	## Features
6	
7	- **Standard Cron Syntax**: Supports both 5-field and 6-field (with seconds) cron expressions
8	- **Timezone-Aware**: Explicit timezone handling to avoid DST surprises
9	- **Middleware Pattern**: Composable job wrappers for logging, metrics, panic recovery, timeouts
10	- **Graceful Shutdown**: Jobs complete cleanly or cancel when context expires
11	- **Zero Dependencies**: Core functionality uses only the standard library
12	- **Type-Safe**: Strong typing with clear error messages
13	- **Well-Tested**: Comprehensive test coverage
14	
15	## Installation
16	
17	This package is included with Memos. No separate installation required.
18	
19	## Quick Start
20	
21	```go
22	package main
23	
24	import (
25	    "context"
26	    "fmt"
27	    "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"
28	)
29	
30	func main() {
31	    s := scheduler.New()
32	
33	    s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
34	        Name:     "daily-cleanup",
35	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *", // 2 AM daily
36	        Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
37	            fmt.Println("Running cleanup...")
38	            return nil
39	        },
40	    })
41	
42	    s.Start()
43	    defer s.Stop(context.Background())
44	
45	    // Keep running...
46	    select {}
47	}
48	```

50	## Cron Expression Format
51	
52	### 5-Field Format (Standard)
53	```
54	┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
55	│ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
56	│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
57	│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
58	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7) (Sunday = 0 or 7)
59	│ │ │ │ │
60	* * * * *
61	```
62	
63	### 6-Field Format (With Seconds)
64	```
65	┌───────────── second (0 - 59)
66	│ ┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
67	│ │ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
68	│ │ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
69	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
70	│ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7)
71	│ │ │ │ │ │
72	* * * * * *
73	```
74	
75	### Special Characters
76	
77	- `*` - Any value (every minute, every hour, etc.)
78	- `,` - List of values: `1,15,30` (1st, 15th, and 30th)
79	- `-` - Range: `9-17` (9 AM through 5 PM)
80	- `/` - Step: `*/15` (every 15 units)
81	
82	### Common Examples
83	
84	| Schedule | Description |
85	|----------|-------------|
86	| `* * * * *` | Every minute |
87	| `0 * * * *` | Every hour |
88	| `0 0 * * *` | Daily at midnight |
89	| `0 9 * * 1-5` | Weekdays at 9 AM |
90	| `*/15 * * * *` | Every 15 minutes |
91	| `0 0 1 * *` | First day of every month |
92	| `0 0 * * 0` | Every Sunday at midnight |
93	| `30 14 * * *` | Every day at 2:30 PM |
94	
95	## Timezone Support
96	
97	```go
98	// Global timezone for all jobs
99	s := scheduler.New(
100	    scheduler.WithTimezone("America/New_York"),
101	)
102	
103	// Per-job timezone (overrides global)
104	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
105	    Name:     "tokyo-report",
106	    Schedule: "0 9 * * *", // 9 AM Tokyo time
107	    Timezone: "Asia/Tokyo",
108	    Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
109	        // Runs at 9 AM in Tokyo
110	        return nil
111	    },
112	})
113	```
114	
115	**Important**: Always use IANA timezone names (`America/New_York`, not `EST`).

117	## Middleware
118	
119	Middleware wraps job handlers to add cross-cutting behavior. Multiple middleware can be chained together.
120	
121	### Built-in Middleware
122	
123	#### Recovery (Panic Handling)
124	
125	```go
126	s := scheduler.New(
127	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
128	        scheduler.Recovery(func(jobName string, r interface{}) {
129	            log.Printf("Job %s panicked: %v", jobName, r)
130	        }),
131	    ),
132	)
133	```
134	
135	#### Logging
136	
137	```go
138	type Logger interface {
139	    Info(msg string, args ...interface{})
140	    Error(msg string, args ...interface{})
141	}
142	
143	s := scheduler.New(
144	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
145	        scheduler.Logging(myLogger),
146	    ),
147	)
148	```
149	
150	#### Timeout
151	
152	```go
153	s := scheduler.New(
154	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
155	        scheduler.Timeout(5 * time.Minute),
156	    ),
157	)
158	```
159	
160	### Combining Middleware
161	
162	```go
163	s := scheduler.New(
164	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
165	        scheduler.Recovery(panicHandler),
166	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
167	        scheduler.Timeout(10 * time.Minute),
168	    ),
169	)
170	```
171	
172	**Order matters**: Middleware are applied left-to-right. In the example above:
173	1. Recovery (outermost) catches panics from everything
174	2. Logging logs the execution
175	3. Timeout (innermost) wraps the actual handler
176	
177	### Custom Middleware
178	
179	```go
180	func Metrics(recorder MetricsRecorder) scheduler.Middleware {
181	    return func(next scheduler.JobHandler) scheduler.JobHandler {
182	        return func(ctx context.Context) error {
183	            start := time.Now()
184	            err := next(ctx)
185	            duration := time.Since(start)
186	
187	            jobName := scheduler.GetJobName(ctx)
188	            recorder.Record(jobName, duration, err)
189	
190	            return err
191	        }
192	    }
193	}
194	```

196	## Graceful Shutdown
197	
198	Always use `Stop()` with a context to allow jobs to finish cleanly:
199	
200	```go
201	// Give jobs up to 30 seconds to complete
202	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
203	defer cancel()
204	
205	if err := s.Stop(ctx); err != nil {
206	    log.Printf("Shutdown error: %v", err)
207	}
208	```
209	
210	Jobs should respect context cancellation:
211	
212	```go
213	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
214	    for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
215	        select {
216	        case <-ctx.Done():
217	            return ctx.Err() // Canceled
218	        default:
219	            // Do work
220	        }
221	    }
222	    return nil
223	}
224	```

226	## Best Practices
227	
228	### 1. Always Name Your Jobs
229	
230	Names are used for logging, metrics, and debugging:
231	
232	```go
233	Name: "user-cleanup-job" // Good
234	Name: "job1"             // Bad
235	```
236	
237	### 2. Add Descriptions and Tags
238	
239	```go
240	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
241	    Name:        "stale-session-cleanup",
242	    Description: "Removes user sessions older than 30 days",
243	    Tags:        []string{"maintenance", "security"},
244	    Schedule:    "0 3 * * *",
245	    Handler:     cleanupSessions,
246	})
247	```
248	
249	### 3. Use Appropriate Middleware
250	
251	Always include Recovery and Logging in production:
252	
253	```go
254	scheduler.New(
255	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
256	        scheduler.Recovery(logPanic),
257	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
258	    ),
259	)
260	```
261	
262	### 4. Avoid Scheduling Exactly on the Hour
263	
264	Many systems schedule jobs at `:00`, causing load spikes. Stagger your jobs:
265	
266	```go
267	"5 2 * * *"  // 2:05 AM (good)
268	"0 2 * * *"  // 2:00 AM (often overloaded)
269	```
270	
271	### 5. Make Jobs Idempotent
272	
273	Jobs may run multiple times (crash recovery, etc.). Design them to be safely re-runnable:
274	
275	```go
276	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
277	    // Use unique constraint or check-before-insert
278	    db.Exec("INSERT IGNORE INTO processed_items ...")
279	    return nil
280	}
281	```
282	
283	### 6. Handle Timezones Explicitly
284	
285	Always specify timezone for business-hour jobs:
286	
287	```go
288	Timezone: "America/New_York" // Good
289	// Timezone: ""              // Bad (defaults to UTC)
290	```
291	
292	### 7. Test Your Cron Expressions
293	
294	Use a cron expression calculator before deploying:
295	- [crontab.guru](https://crontab.guru/)
296	- Write unit tests with the parser
297

44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})
70	
71		// Serve frontend static files.
72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
82		fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
83	
84		// Create and register RSS routes (needs markdown service from apiV1Service).
85		rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
86	
87		// Register gRPC gateway as api v1 (includes SSE endpoint on CORS-enabled group).
88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")
90		}
91	
92		mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
95		}
96		mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
97	
98		return s, nil
99	}

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}
133	
134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {
147			slog.Error("failed to close database", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
148		}
149	
150		slog.Info("memos stopped properly")

11	// reservedCIDRs lists IP ranges that must never be targeted by outbound webhook requests.
12	// Covers loopback, RFC-1918 private, link-local (including cloud IMDS at 169.254.169.254),
13	// and their IPv6 equivalents.

15		"127.0.0.0/8",    // IPv4 loopback
16		"10.0.0.0/8",     // RFC-1918 class A
17		"172.16.0.0/12",  // RFC-1918 class B
18		"192.168.0.0/16", // RFC-1918 class C
19		"169.254.0.0/16", // Link-local / cloud IMDS
20		"::1/128",        // IPv6 loopback
21		"fc00::/7",       // IPv6 unique local

25	// reservedNetworks is the parsed form of reservedCIDRs, built once at startup.

28	func init() {

126		}
127	
128		// Get existing webhooks
129		webhooks, err := s.Store.GetUserWebhooks(ctx, userID)
130		if err != nil {
131			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user webhooks: %v", err)
132		}
133	
134		// Find the webhook to update
135		var targetWebhook *storepb.WebhooksUserSetting_Webhook

137			if webhook.Id == webhookID {
138				targetWebhook = webhook
139				break
140			}
141		}
142

144			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "webhook not found")
145		}

148		updatedWebhook := &storepb.WebhooksUserSetting_Webhook{
149			Id:            webhookID,

155		if request.UpdateMask != nil {
156			for _, path := range request.UpdateMask.Paths {
157				switch path {
158				case "url":

160						trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(request.Webhook.Url)

163						}
164						updatedWebhook.Url = trimmed
165					}
166				case "display_name":
167					updatedWebhook.Title = request.Webhook.DisplayName
168				case "signing_secret":
169					secret := strings.TrimSpace(request.Webhook.SigningSecret)
170					if err := webhook.ValidateSigningSecret(secret); err != nil {
171						return nil, err
172					}
173					updatedWebhook.SigningSecret = secret
174				default:
175					// Ignore unsupported fields
176				}
177			}
178		} else {
179			// If no update mask is provided, update all fields
180			if request.Webhook.Url != "" {
181				trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(request.Webhook.Url)
182				if err := webhook.ValidateURL(trimmed); err != nil {
183					return nil, err
184				}
185				updatedWebhook.Url = trimmed
186			}
187			updatedWebhook.Title = request.Webhook.DisplayName
188			if request.Webhook.SigningSecret != "" {
189				secret := strings.TrimSpace(request.Webhook.SigningSecret)
190				if err := webhook.ValidateSigningSecret(secret); err != nil {
191					return nil, err
192				}
193				updatedWebhook.SigningSecret = secret
194			}
195		}
196	
197		err = s.Store.UpdateUserWebhook(ctx, userID, updatedWebhook)
198		if err != nil {
199			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to update webhook: %v", err)
200		}
201

203	}

88	func TestPostSignsRequest(t *testing.T) {
89		// httptest listens on 127.0.0.1, which the SSRF guard blocks by default.
90		prev := AllowPrivateIPs
91		AllowPrivateIPs = true

93

95		cases := []struct {
96			name   string
97			secret string
98			key    []byte
99		}{
100			{name: "plain secret", secret: "plain-secret-value", key: []byte("plain-secret-value")},
101			{name: "whsec_ secret", secret: "whsec_" + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(rawKey), key: rawKey},
102		}
103	
104		for _, tc := range cases {
105			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
106				var gotID, gotTimestamp, gotSignature string
107				var gotBody []byte
108				server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
109					gotID = r.Header.Get("webhook-id")
110					gotTimestamp = r.Header.Get("webhook-timestamp")
111					gotSignature = r.Header.Get("webhook-signature")
112					gotBody, _ = io.ReadAll(r.Body)
113					_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"code":0}`))
114				}))
115				defer server.Close()
116	
117				err := Post(&WebhookRequestPayload{
118					URL:           server.URL,
119					ActivityType:  "memos.memo.created",
120					Creator:       "users/1",
121					SigningSecret: tc.secret,
122				})
123				require.NoError(t, err)
124	
125				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotID, "msg_"), "webhook-id should be prefixed with msg_")
126				require.NotEmpty(t, gotTimestamp)
127				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotSignature, "v1,"), "signature should carry the v1 version tag")
128	
129				// Recompute the signature the way a receiver would and confirm it matches.
130				mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, tc.key)
131				mac.Write([]byte(gotID + "." + gotTimestamp + "."))
132				mac.Write(gotBody)
133				want := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
134				require.Equal(t, "v1,"+want, gotSignature)
135			})
136		}
137	}

44		// Archived memos are only visible to their creator.
45		if memo.RowStatus == store.Archived {

47			if err != nil {
48				return status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user")
49			}

51				return status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "memo not found")

56			user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)

60			if user == nil {

62			}

20	func (s *APIV1Service) CreateMemoComment(ctx context.Context, request *v1pb.CreateMemoCommentRequest) (*v1pb.Memo, error) {
21		memoUID, err := ExtractMemoUIDFromName(request.Name)
22		if err != nil {
23			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid memo name: %v", err)
24		}
25		relatedMemo, err := s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{UID: &memoUID})
26		if err != nil {
27			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get memo")
28		}
29		if relatedMemo == nil {
30			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "memo not found")
31		}
32	
33		// Check memo visibility before allowing comment.
34		user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
35		if err != nil {
36			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user")
37		}
38		if user == nil {
39			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not authenticated")
40		}
41		if relatedMemo.Visibility == store.Private && relatedMemo.CreatorID != user.ID && !isSuperUser(user) {
42			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
43		}
44		if request.Comment == nil {
45			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "comment is required")
46		}
47	
48		comment, ok := proto.Clone(request.Comment).(*v1pb.Memo)
49		if !ok {
50			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to clone memo comment")
51		}
52		comment.Visibility = convertVisibilityFromStore(relatedMemo.Visibility)
53	
54		// Create the memo comment first; suppress the generic memo.created SSE event
55		// since CreateMemoComment broadcasts memo.comment.created for the parent instead.
56		memoComment, err := s.CreateMemo(withSuppressMentionNotifications(withSuppressSSE(ctx)), &v1pb.CreateMemoRequest{
57			Memo:   comment,
58			MemoId: request.CommentId,
59		})
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to create memo")
62		}
63		memoUID, err = ExtractMemoUIDFromName(memoComment.Name)
64		if err != nil {
65			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid memo name: %v", err)
66		}
67		memo, err := s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{UID: &memoUID})
68		if err != nil {
69			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get memo")
70		}
71	
72		// Build the relation between the comment memo and the original memo.
73		_, err = s.Store.UpsertMemoRelation(ctx, &store.MemoRelation{
74			MemoID:        memo.ID,
75			RelatedMemoID: relatedMemo.ID,
76			Type:          store.MemoRelationComment,
77		})
78		if err != nil {

80		}
81

85		// to the parent memo.
86		relations, err := s.loadMemoRelations(ctx, memo)
87		if err != nil {
88			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to load memo relations")
89		}

91

93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid memo creator")
95		}
96		if creator == nil {
97			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "memo creator not found")
98		}
99		creatorID := creator.ID

101			if _, err := s.createInboxWithEmailNotification(ctx, &store.Inbox{
102				SenderID:   creatorID,
103				ReceiverID: relatedMemo.CreatorID,
104				Status:     store.UNREAD,
105				Message: &storepb.InboxMessage{
106					Type: storepb.InboxMessage_MEMO_COMMENT,
107					Payload: &storepb.InboxMessage_MemoComment{
108						MemoComment: &storepb.InboxMessage_MemoCommentPayload{
109							MemoId:        memo.ID,
110							RelatedMemoId: relatedMemo.ID,
111						},
112					},
113				},
114			}); err != nil {
115				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to create inbox")
116			}
117		}
118	
119		if err := s.DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook(ctx, memoComment, relatedMemo.CreatorID); err != nil {
120			slog.Warn("Failed to dispatch memo comment created webhook", slog.Any("err", err))

122

57	// safeDialContext is a net.Dialer.DialContext replacement that resolves the target

59	func safeDialContext(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error) {

92	// resolveSigningKey returns the raw HMAC key for a signing secret. Secrets using
93	// the Standard Webhooks "whsec_<base64>" serialization are base64-decoded to their

97	func resolveSigningKey(secret string) ([]byte, error) {
98		if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(secret, "whsec_"); ok {
99			decoded, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(rest)

126		req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", requestPayload.URL, bytes.NewBuffer(body))
127		if err != nil {
128			return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to construct webhook request to %s", requestPayload.URL)
129		}

131		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
132	
133		if requestPayload.SigningSecret != "" {
134			key, err := resolveSigningKey(requestPayload.SigningSecret)

137			}

142			mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
143			mac.Write([]byte(msgID + "." + timestamp + "."))
144			mac.Write(body)
145			signature := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))

32			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not authenticated")

35			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")

102		}
103	
104		for _, tc := range cases {
105			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
106				var gotID, gotTimestamp, gotSignature string
107				var gotBody []byte
108				server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
109					gotID = r.Header.Get("webhook-id")
110					gotTimestamp = r.Header.Get("webhook-timestamp")
111					gotSignature = r.Header.Get("webhook-signature")
112					gotBody, _ = io.ReadAll(r.Body)

114				}))

121					SigningSecret: tc.secret,

132				mac.Write(gotBody)

## Summary of Webhook and Outbound HTTP Delivery Security Analysis

Based on my thorough search of the codebase, here are the findings regarding outbound HTTP delivery, webhooks, and SSRF protection mechanisms:

### 1. **Webhook Execution and HTTP Delivery**

- `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go` - Core webhook dispatch and HTTP execution

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` - Memo-related webhook dispatching

**Webhook Dispatch Mechanism:**
- Webhooks are dispatched via `webhook.Post()` (synchronous) and `webhook.PostAsync()` (async to queue) functions
- Asynchronous dispatch uses a bounded queue (128 size limit) with 4 worker goroutines
- Webhooks are triggered on memo create, update, delete, and comment events
- Dispatch is logged as warnings on failure but doesn't block the main operation

**Key Webhook Types:**
- `memos.memo.created` - triggered when memo is created
- `memos.memo.updated` - triggered when memo is updated
- `memos.memo.deleted` - triggered when memo is deleted
- `memos.memo.comment.created` - triggered when a comment is created on a memo

### 2. **SSRF Protection Mechanisms**

**Comprehensive SSRF Defense:**

The codebase implements layered SSRF protection:

1. **Custom HTTP Transport** (`safeClient` at line 32-37 of webhook.go):
   - Uses custom `DialContext: safeDialContext` to intercept all connections
   - All webhook requests use this protected client exclusively

2. **Safe Dial Context** (`safeDialContext` at lines 57-77 of webhook.go):
   - Resolves hostname via DNS
   - Validates **every resolved IP address** against reserved/private ranges
   - Blocks connection if ANY resolved IP falls in blocked ranges
   - Defeats DNS rebinding attacks by validating at connection time

3. **Reserved IP CIDR Blocks** (lines 14-23 of validate.go):
   ```
   - 127.0.0.0/8       (IPv4 loopback)
   - 10.0.0.0/8        (RFC-1918 private)
   - 172.16.0.0/12     (RFC-1918 private)
   - 192.168.0.0/16    (RFC-1918 private)
   - 169.254.0.0/16    (Link-local/cloud IMDS)
   - ::1/128           (IPv6 loopback)
   - fc00::/7          (IPv6 unique local)
   - fe80::/10         (IPv6 link-local)
   ```

4. **URL Validation** (`ValidateURL` at lines 56-83 of validate.go):
   - Validates URL is properly formatted (ParseRequestURI)
   - Enforces HTTP/HTTPS schemes only
   - Performs DNS lookup to resolve hostname
   - Checks all resolved IPs against reserved ranges
   - Returns gRPC InvalidArgument status on failure

### 3. **Configuration and Bypass Control**

**AllowPrivateIPs Flag:**
- Defined at line 41 of validate.go as a package-level boolean
- **Default: false** (strict SSRF protection enabled)
- Controlled by CLI flag `--allow-private-webhooks` (cmd/memos/main.go:133)
- Environment variable: `MEMOS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_WEBHOOKS`
- Set at initialization (cmd/memos/main.go:49): `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs = viper.GetBool("allow-private-webhooks")`
- When true, disables SSRF protection (line 45-46 of validate.go)
- Intended for self-hosted deployments with local network webhooks

### 4. **Webhook Signature and Authentication**

**Standard Webhooks Compliance:**
- Uses Standard Webhooks "whsec_" format (base64-encoded 32-byte key)
- HMAC-SHA256 signatures with headers:
  - `webhook-id`: "msg_" prefixed UUID
  - `webhook-timestamp`: Unix timestamp
  - `webhook-signature`: "v1," + base64-encoded signature
- Signing secret validation (lines 90-103 of validate.go)
- Rejects control characters (\r, \n, \t) and non-ASCII in signing secrets

### 5. **Other HTTP Operations with Security**

- Uses separate `secureDialContext` for fetching open graph metadata
- Implements same IP validation as webhooks (line 104-106: `isInternalIP` function)

- **SECURITY ISSUE**: Uses `http.Get()` directly without validation (line 21)
- Does NOT validate URLs before making requests
- No SSRF protection - vulnerable to SSRF if called with attacker-controlled URLs

- HTML meta fetching timeout: **5 seconds** (line 38 of html_meta.go)
- Async queue capacity: **128 entries** with 4 workers
- Response body reading limited to 1MB (line 158 of webhook.go)

**Configuration:**
- User webhooks created/updated/deleted via gRPC API with `ValidateURL` checks

26	// NewIdentityProvider initializes a new OAuth2 Identity Provider with the given configuration.
27	func NewIdentityProvider(config *storepb.OAuth2Config) (*IdentityProvider, error) {
28		for v, field := range map[string]string{

30			config.ClientSecret:            "clientSecret",
31			config.TokenUrl:                "tokenUrl",
32			config.UserInfoUrl:             "userInfoUrl",

46	// If codeVerifier is provided, it will be used for PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) validation.
47	func (p *IdentityProvider) ExchangeToken(ctx context.Context, redirectURL, code, codeVerifier string) (string, error) {
48		conf := &oauth2.Config{
49			ClientID:     p.config.ClientId,
50			ClientSecret: p.config.ClientSecret,
51			RedirectURL:  redirectURL,
52			Scopes:       p.config.Scopes,
53			Endpoint: oauth2.Endpoint{
54				AuthURL:   p.config.AuthUrl,
55				TokenURL:  p.config.TokenUrl,
56				AuthStyle: oauth2.AuthStyleAutoDetect,
57			},
58		}
59	
60		// Prepare token exchange options
61		opts := []oauth2.AuthCodeOption{}
62	
63		// Add PKCE code_verifier if provided
64		if codeVerifier != "" {
65			opts = append(opts, oauth2.SetAuthURLParam("code_verifier", codeVerifier))
66		}
67	
68		token, err := conf.Exchange(ctx, code, opts...)
69		if err != nil {
70			return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to exchange access token")
71		}
72	
73		// Use the standard AccessToken field instead of Extra()
74		// This is more reliable across different OAuth providers
75		if token.AccessToken == "" {
76			return "", errors.New("missing access token from authorization response")
77		}
78	
79		return token.AccessToken, nil

92		if err != nil {
93			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get user information")
94		}

97		if resp.StatusCode < http.StatusOK || resp.StatusCode >= http.StatusMultipleChoices {

54	func (s *Store) ListIdentityProviders(ctx context.Context, find *FindIdentityProvider) ([]*storepb.IdentityProvider, error) {

61		if find.ID != nil {

64		if find.UID != nil {

88		for _, provider := range deploymentProviders {

84		}
85		if currentUser == nil {

87		}
88		if currentUser.Role != store.RoleAdmin {
89			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
90		}
91	
92		if request.UpdateMask == nil || len(request.UpdateMask.Paths) == 0 {
93			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "update_mask is required")
94		}
95	
96		uid, err := ExtractIdentityProviderUIDFromName(request.IdentityProvider.Name)
97		if err != nil {

99		}
100		if s.Store.IsIdentityProviderDeploymentConfigured(uid) {
101			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.FailedPrecondition, "identity provider %q is configured by the deployment", uid)
102		}
103	
104		// Look up the IdP by UID to get the internal ID for update.
105		existing, err := s.Store.GetStoredIdentityProvider(ctx, &store.FindIdentityProvider{UID: &uid})
106		if err != nil {
107			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get identity provider, error: %+v", err)

110			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "identity provider not found")

114			ID:   existing.Id,

116		}
117		for _, field := range request.UpdateMask.Paths {
118			switch field {
119			case "title":
120				update.Name = &request.IdentityProvider.Title

19	func (s *APIV1Service) resolveSSOUser(ctx context.Context, currentUser *store.User, identityProvider *storepb.IdentityProvider, userInfo *idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo) (*store.User, error) {
20		provider := identityProvider.Uid
21		externUID := userInfo.Identifier
22	
23		user, err := s.getLinkedSSOUser(ctx, provider, externUID)
24		if err != nil {
25			return nil, err
26		}
27		if user != nil {
28			if currentUser != nil && currentUser.ID != user.ID {
29				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.AlreadyExists, "identity provider account is already linked to another user")
30			}
31			return user, nil
32		}
33	
34		if currentUser != nil {
35			return s.bindSSOIdentityToUser(ctx, currentUser, provider, externUID)
36		}
37	
38		// Miss path: enforce the registration gate before creating anything.
39		instanceGeneralSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceGeneralSetting(ctx)
40		if err != nil {
41			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get instance general setting, error: %v", err)
42		}
43		if instanceGeneralSetting.DisallowUserRegistration {
44			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "user registration is not allowed")
45		}
46	
47		password, err := util.RandomString(20)
48		if err != nil {
49			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to generate random password, error: %v", err)
50		}

52		if err != nil {
53			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to generate password hash, error: %v", err)
54		}
55		username, err := deriveSSOUsername()
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to derive username, error: %v", err)
58		}
59		user, err = s.Store.CreateUser(ctx, &store.User{
60			Username:     username,
61			Role:         store.RoleUser,
62			Nickname:     userInfo.DisplayName,
63			Email:        userInfo.Email,
64			AvatarURL:    userInfo.AvatarURL,
65			PasswordHash: string(passwordHash),
66		})
67		if err != nil {
68			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to create user, error: %v", err)
69		}
70	
71		if _, err := s.Store.CreateUserIdentity(ctx, &store.UserIdentity{
72			UserID:    user.ID,
73			Provider:  provider,
74			ExternUID: externUID,
75		}); err != nil {
76			// Best-effort cleanup: the provisional user row has no linkage and should not remain.
77			_, _ = s.Store.DeleteUser(ctx, &store.DeleteUser{ID: user.ID})
78			if isUniqueConstraintViolation(err) {
79				// Concurrent first login won the race; load the winning linkage's user.
80				winner, getErr := s.Store.GetUserIdentity(ctx, &store.FindUserIdentity{
81					Provider:  &provider,
82					ExternUID: &externUID,
83				})
84				if getErr != nil {
85					return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to reload user identity after race, error: %v", getErr)
86				}
87				if winner == nil {
88					return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "user identity conflict reported but no winning row found")
89				}
90				winnerUser, getErr := s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{ID: &winner.UserID})
91				if getErr != nil {
92					return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user after race, error: %v", getErr)
93				}
94				if winnerUser == nil {
95					return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "linked user %d not found after race", winner.UserID)
96				}
97				return winnerUser, nil
98			}
99			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to create user identity, error: %v", err)
100		}
101		return user, nil
102	}

104	func (s *APIV1Service) resolveSSOIdentity(ctx context.Context, idpName, code, redirectURI, codeVerifier string) (*storepb.IdentityProvider, *idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo, error) {
105		idpUID, err := ExtractIdentityProviderUIDFromName(idpName)
106		if err != nil {
107			return nil, nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid identity provider name: %v", err)
108		}
109		identityProvider, err := s.Store.GetIdentityProvider(ctx, &store.FindIdentityProvider{
110			UID: &idpUID,
111		})
112		if err != nil {
113			return nil, nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get identity provider, error: %v", err)
114		}
115		if identityProvider == nil {
116			return nil, nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "identity provider not found")
117		}
118	
119		var userInfo *idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo
120		if identityProvider.Type == storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2 {
121			oauth2IdentityProvider, err := oauth2.NewIdentityProvider(identityProvider.Config.GetOauth2Config())
122			if err != nil {
123				return nil, nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to create oauth2 identity provider, error: %v", err)
124			}
125			// Pass code_verifier for PKCE support (empty string if not provided for backward compatibility)
126			token, err := oauth2IdentityProvider.ExchangeToken(ctx, redirectURI, code, codeVerifier)
127			if err != nil {
128				return nil, nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to exchange token, error: %v", err)
129			}
130			userInfo, err = oauth2IdentityProvider.UserInfo(ctx, token)
131			if err != nil {
132				return nil, nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user info, error: %v", err)
133			}
134		}
135	
136		identifierFilter := identityProvider.IdentifierFilter
137		if identifierFilter != "" {
138			identifierFilterRegex, err := regexp.Compile(identifierFilter)
139			if err != nil {
140				return nil, nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to compile identifier filter regex, error: %v", err)
141			}
142			if !identifierFilterRegex.MatchString(userInfo.Identifier) {
143				return nil, nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "identifier %s is not allowed", userInfo.Identifier)
144			}
145		}
146	
147		return identityProvider, userInfo, nil
148	}

154		})
155		if err != nil {
156			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user identity, error: %v", err)
157		}
158		if identity == nil {
159			return nil, nil
160		}
161		user, err := s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{ID: &identity.UserID})
162		if err != nil {
163			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user, error: %v", err)
164		}
165		if user == nil {
166			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "linked user %d not found for identity %d", identity.UserID, identity.ID)
167		}

224	// isUniqueConstraintViolation matches the driver-specific error messages that each
225	// supported backend emits when any UNIQUE constraint rejects an insert. Callers
226	// disambiguate which constraint was hit from the insertion context (e.g. inserting
227	// a user_identity row can only violate UNIQUE(provider, extern_uid); inserting a
228	// user row can only violate UNIQUE(username)). Matches the pattern used in
229	// memo_service.go for the memo UID unique check.
230	func isUniqueConstraintViolation(err error) bool {
231		if err == nil {
232			return false
233		}
234		msg := err.Error()
235		return strings.Contains(msg, "UNIQUE constraint failed") ||
236			strings.Contains(msg, "duplicate key") ||

26	// NewIdentityProvider initializes a new OAuth2 Identity Provider with the given configuration.
27	func NewIdentityProvider(config *storepb.OAuth2Config) (*IdentityProvider, error) {
28		for v, field := range map[string]string{
29			config.ClientId:                "clientId",
30			config.ClientSecret:            "clientSecret",
31			config.TokenUrl:                "tokenUrl",
32			config.UserInfoUrl:             "userInfoUrl",
33			config.FieldMapping.Identifier: "fieldMapping.identifier",
34		} {
35			if v == "" {
36				return nil, errors.Errorf(`the field "%s" is empty but required`, field)
37			}
38		}
39	
40		return &IdentityProvider{
41			config: config,
42		}, nil
43	}

45	// ExchangeToken returns the exchanged OAuth2 token using the given authorization code.
46	// If codeVerifier is provided, it will be used for PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) validation.
47	func (p *IdentityProvider) ExchangeToken(ctx context.Context, redirectURL, code, codeVerifier string) (string, error) {
48		conf := &oauth2.Config{
49			ClientID:     p.config.ClientId,
50			ClientSecret: p.config.ClientSecret,
51			RedirectURL:  redirectURL,
52			Scopes:       p.config.Scopes,
53			Endpoint: oauth2.Endpoint{
54				AuthURL:   p.config.AuthUrl,
55				TokenURL:  p.config.TokenUrl,
56				AuthStyle: oauth2.AuthStyleAutoDetect,
57			},
58		}
59	
60		// Prepare token exchange options
61		opts := []oauth2.AuthCodeOption{}
62	
63		// Add PKCE code_verifier if provided
64		if codeVerifier != "" {
65			opts = append(opts, oauth2.SetAuthURLParam("code_verifier", codeVerifier))
66		}
67	
68		token, err := conf.Exchange(ctx, code, opts...)
69		if err != nil {
70			return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to exchange access token")
71		}
72	
73		// Use the standard AccessToken field instead of Extra()
74		// This is more reliable across different OAuth providers
75		if token.AccessToken == "" {
76			return "", errors.New("missing access token from authorization response")
77		}
78	
79		return token.AccessToken, nil
80	}

82	// UserInfo returns the parsed user information using the given OAuth2 token.
83	func (p *IdentityProvider) UserInfo(ctx context.Context, token string) (*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo, error) {
84		client := &http.Client{Timeout: userInfoRequestTimeout}
85		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, p.config.UserInfoUrl, nil)
86		if err != nil {
87			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create http request")
88		}
89		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
90		req.Header.Set("Authorization", fmt.Sprintf("Bearer %s", token))
91		resp, err := client.Do(req)
92		if err != nil {
93			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get user information")
94		}
95		defer resp.Body.Close()
96	
97		if resp.StatusCode < http.StatusOK || resp.StatusCode >= http.StatusMultipleChoices {
98			body, readErr := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 4096))
99			if readErr != nil {
100				return nil, errors.Wrap(readErr, "failed to read error response body")
101			}
102			return nil, errors.Errorf("userinfo request failed with status %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, string(body))
103		}
104	
105		body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
106		if err != nil {
107			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read response body")
108		}
109	
110		var claims map[string]any
111		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &claims); err != nil {
112			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to unmarshal response body")
113		}

116			userInfo.Identifier = v
117		}
118		if userInfo.Identifier == "" {
119			return nil, errors.Errorf("the field %q is not found in claims or has empty value", p.config.FieldMapping.Identifier)

122		// Best effort to map optional fields

124			if v, ok := claims[p.config.FieldMapping.DisplayName].(string); ok {
125				userInfo.DisplayName = v

54	func (s *Store) ListIdentityProviders(ctx context.Context, find *FindIdentityProvider) ([]*storepb.IdentityProvider, error) {
55		stored, err := s.listStoredIdentityProviders(ctx, find)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, err
58		}
59		// File-backed providers do not have database IDs. ID-filtered reads are raw
60		// stored-resource lookups used by mutation paths.
61		if find.ID != nil {
62			return stored, nil
63		}
64		if find.UID != nil {
65			if provider := s.getDeploymentIdentityProvider(*find.UID); provider != nil {
66				return []*storepb.IdentityProvider{provider}, nil
67			}
68			return stored, nil
69		}
70	
71		deploymentProviders := s.listDeploymentIdentityProviders()
72		deploymentByUID := make(map[string]*storepb.IdentityProvider, len(deploymentProviders))
73		for _, provider := range deploymentProviders {
74			deploymentByUID[provider.Uid] = provider
75		}
76		identityProviders := make([]*storepb.IdentityProvider, 0, len(stored)+len(deploymentProviders))
77		for _, provider := range stored {
78			if configured := deploymentByUID[provider.Uid]; configured != nil {
79				identityProviders = append(identityProviders, configured)
80				delete(deploymentByUID, provider.Uid)
81				continue
82			}
83			identityProviders = append(identityProviders, provider)
84		}
85		// listDeploymentIdentityProviders is UID-sorted, so providers that exist
86		// only in deployment configuration are appended deterministically without
87		// reordering existing database-backed providers.
88		for _, provider := range deploymentProviders {
89			if deploymentByUID[provider.Uid] != nil {
90				identityProviders = append(identityProviders, provider)
91			}
92		}
93		return identityProviders, nil
94	}

81		currentUser, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
82		if err != nil {

85		if currentUser == nil {

91	
92		if request.UpdateMask == nil || len(request.UpdateMask.Paths) == 0 {
93			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "update_mask is required")

95	
96		uid, err := ExtractIdentityProviderUIDFromName(request.IdentityProvider.Name)

100		if s.Store.IsIdentityProviderDeploymentConfigured(uid) {
101			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.FailedPrecondition, "identity provider %q is configured by the deployment", uid)
102		}
103	
104		// Look up the IdP by UID to get the internal ID for update.
105		existing, err := s.Store.GetStoredIdentityProvider(ctx, &store.FindIdentityProvider{UID: &uid})
106		if err != nil {
107			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get identity provider, error: %+v", err)
108		}
109		if existing == nil {
110			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "identity provider not found")
111		}
112	
113		update := &store.UpdateIdentityProviderV1{
114			ID:   existing.Id,
115			Type: storepb.IdentityProvider_Type(storepb.IdentityProvider_Type_value[request.IdentityProvider.Type.String()]),
116		}
117		for _, field := range request.UpdateMask.Paths {
118			switch field {
119			case "title":
120				update.Name = &request.IdentityProvider.Title
121			case "identifier_filter":
122				update.IdentifierFilter = &request.IdentityProvider.IdentifierFilter
123			case "config":

131		if update.Config != nil {

134					oauth2Config.ClientSecret = existingOAuth.ClientSecret
135				}
136			}
137		}
138	
139		identityProvider, err := s.Store.UpdateIdentityProvider(ctx, update)
140		if err != nil {

184	func convertIdentityProviderFromStore(identityProvider *storepb.IdentityProvider) *v1pb.IdentityProvider {
185		temp := &v1pb.IdentityProvider{

188			IdentifierFilter: identityProvider.IdentifierFilter,
189			Type:             v1pb.IdentityProvider_Type(v1pb.IdentityProvider_Type_value[identityProvider.Type.String()]),
190		}
191		if identityProvider.Type == storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2 {
192			oauth2Config := identityProvider.Config.GetOauth2Config()
193			temp.Config = &v1pb.IdentityProviderConfig{
194				Config: &v1pb.IdentityProviderConfig_Oauth2Config{
195					Oauth2Config: &v1pb.OAuth2Config{
196						ClientId: oauth2Config.ClientId,
197						// ClientSecret is write-only: never returned in responses.
198						AuthUrl:     oauth2Config.AuthUrl,

204							DisplayName: oauth2Config.FieldMapping.DisplayName,

206							AvatarUrl:   oauth2Config.FieldMapping.AvatarUrl,

209				},
210			}
211		}
212		return temp
